prices.pack: 400 g — NOT rice_1kg. Scaling this to a kilo would give 12.5, badly wrong versus the 6-7 LYD retail kilo.

prices.says: مكرونة محلية (سباغيتي) | 400 جرام | 3.500 د.ل; مكرونة محلية (لوبيا) 400 جرام 4.000; مكرونة مستوردة 400 جرام 5.000
prices.pack: 400 g — NOT pasta_500g

prices.says: دقيق المخابز (الناعم) | قنطار واحد | 270 د.ل — also دقيق المخابز (السميد) قنطار 242 د.ل and دقيق المخابز (الربع) قنطار 256 د.ل
prices.pack: 1 قنطار of BAKERY flour ≈ 100 kg (see pack_words) — NOT a 50 kg sack. Left unlabelled on purpose: the merge must decide whether to derive bakery_flour_50kg from it, and if so it is roughly half, ~135 LYD.

dialect.gloss: carton — the wholesale unit for pads
dialect.note: 'ليلاس الكبير كرتونه 100 دينار فيها 12 كيس' — one carton = 12 كيس. Also spelled كرتونه without the ة.

dialect.gloss: bag — the retail pack unit for pads
dialect.note: A كرتونة contains 12 كيس; a shopper buys one كيس.
'فوط نسائيه يوميه البكيت 2ونص فيه 120حبه' — packet of 120 daily liners for 2.5 LYD.

dialect.gloss: 'and a half' — written joined to the number, no space
dialect.note: '2ونص' = 2.5 dinars, '1ونص' = 1.5 dinars. A price parser splitting on whitespace will miss this.

dialect.gloss: one piece — the count word for pads
dialect.note: 'صندوق 24 حبة', 'فوط نسائيه شهريه 25حبه', '120حبه'. Often written with no space before the number and with ه for ة.
'فوط نسائية شهرية قطن 100/100 صندوق 24 حبة'.

dialect.gloss: the sleeve/strip — a shrink-wrapped multipack of soap bars
dialect.note: 'صابون لوكس الاستيكة 5.75 بدلا من 8 دينار' alongside 'صابون صلب لوكس الاصلي 6قطع بسعر التحطيم 5.75دينار' — so one استيكة = 6 bars. Not in the catalogue's pack vocabulary.

dialect.gloss: bar (of soap) — as opposed to سائل (liquid)
dialect.note: Lucky (Libyan manufacturer) files its soap under 'صابون أيادي سائل وقالب'. But قالب صابون also means a soap MOULD — riad.ly sells 'قالب صابون سيلكون ... لصنع الصابون' as a craft item.
The clearest disambiguator from صابون سائل (liquid). 'صابون صلب لوكس الاصلي6قطع'.

dialect.gloss: (a) a bar of soap; (b) Libyan slang for a small router/modem or a device casing
dialect.note: HARD NEGATIVE. Seen as 'صابونة شارب 24 ... سعرها 300 دينار' and 'ركبت الشفرة في صابونة Jio 4g' — these are telecom devices, not soap. Matching on صابونة alone will produce false positives at 300 LYD.
dialect.source: Google SERP for: site:facebook.com "صابونة" ليبيا سعر دينار طرابلس محل — the result links were Google redirect URLs and did not resolve to citable page URLs

dialect.gloss: bath TOWELS — not pads and not soap
dialect.note: HARD NEGATIVE, and the single most dangerous one for this item: 'فوط حمّام ... المقاس 50*90 بسعر 13 دينار'. The word فوط carries both senses; only the modifier separates them.
Another فوط hard negative, sold by cleaning-supplies wholesalers.
Libyan sellers price and pack these as two different products: 'فوط نسائيه يوميه البكيت 2ونص فيه 120حبه' vs 'فوط نسائيه شهريه 25حبه 1ونص'. See notes — يومية should NOT map to sanitary_pads_10.
Standard pad qualifier in Libyan product names; بجوانح is the colloquial variant of بأجنحة.

dialect.gloss: thick / ultra / super / maxi — pad thickness tiers
dialect.note: 'لاكي ليدي ألترا كبير – بالأجنحة سميك'. Latin 'MAXI' also appears untransliterated: 'فوط MAXI Vellia'.
Libyan sale phrasing that sits right next to the number and will confuse a naive price extractor: 'سعرها حرق بنار سعر 100 دينار', 'بسعر التحطيم 5.75دينار'.

dialect.gloss: 'bank-card price is the same as the cash price'
dialect.note: A distinctly Libyan price qualifier — sellers routinely quote two prices (cash vs bank transfer/card) and say so in the post. Where they differ, a scraper may pick the wrong one.

dsm.ly renders 9 LYD as 'د.ل.‏ 9,000'. The comma is a decimal separator here, not a thousands separator — confirmed by the site's own price filter buckets ('1 - 200' holding 42 of 42 items in the pads category).
Very common in Libyan shop posts: 'فوط صحيه ليلاس', 'فوط نسائيه شهريه'. Normalising ه/ة is required or half the real strings miss.
Distinct pad sub-products. 'لاكي ليدي سوبر أمومة', 'الفوط النسائيه لما بعد الولادة', and riad.ly's Lilas variant 'المخصص للنزيف'.

dialect.gloss: Lucky Lady — a Libyan-made pad brand
dialect.note: Made by شركة الربيع القابضة, Tripoli / وادي الربيع. Domestic brand, so likely the cheap end of the market. Sister brands لاكي بيبي (nappies), لاكي أدلت (adult), لاكي فريش, لاكي هوم.

dialect.gloss: Lilas — the dominant imported pad brand in Libya
dialect.note: Has a dedicated Libyan agency page (Lilas Libya - ليلاس ليبيا). Sizes written as 'ليلاس الكبير', 'ليلاس العادي', 'ليلاس سوبر'.

The default Libyan retail word for any liquid medicine. Written after the brand, not before: 'بنادول شراب', 'اوجمنتين شراب', 'ادول شراب'. A Qeema matcher keyed on 'syrup <brand>' word order will miss most Libyan listings.
Appears in importer/manufacturer copy ('معلق شراب', 'باراسيتامول معلق') but almost never in Libyan retail pharmacy posts, which say شراب. Treat معلق as a wholesale-register synonym.
How paediatric paracetamol is actually described and searched for in Libya — far more common than the molecule name. 'دواء الحرارة' ('the fever medicine') is the colloquial form.
The standard qualifier that separates the paediatric liquid from the adult tablet on a Libyan price list. 'بنادول' alone is ambiguous; 'بنادول شراب للرضع و الاطفال' is unambiguously the item.

The full formal name, used with the English abbreviation in brackets: 'محلول معالجة الجفاف (ORS)'. Shortened in trade copy to 'محلول جفاف'. Libyans rarely write 'أملاح الإماهة الفموية' (that is Gulf/Levant register).

Used interchangeably with أكياس / كيس. Trade copy writes 'ساشت (عبوة 10 أكياس)' — sachet, pack of 10 bags. So a Qeema matcher for ors_sachet should accept ساشت, كيس, أكياس and the plain English 'sachet'.

dialect.gloss: Rehydran — a named ORS sachet brand used in Libyan paediatric practice
dialect.note: Written as 'أكياس محلول معالجة الجفاف ريهيدران Rehydran Packs' with dosing 'كيس على 200 مل مياه سبق غليها' (one sachet to 200 ml of pre-boiled water). This is the concrete brand behind the generic ors_sachet item in Libya.

dialect.gloss: 'at a price of' — the price marker in Libyan pharmacy posts
dialect.note: Almost every Libyan pharmacy price line is 'X بسعر N دينار فقط' or 'السعر N دينار'. The trailing فقط ('only') is near-obligatory in ad copy. Ranges are written bare with a hyphen: 'بسعر 15-20 دينار فقط'. Also seen: '#السعر5دينار' with no spaces, glued into a hashtag.

dialect.gloss: 20.000 LYD — the comma is a DECIMAL separator, not a thousands separator
dialect.note: CRITICAL PARSING TRAP. Libya's largest online pharmacy (dsm.ly) renders every price as 'د.ل.‏ N,000' with three decimal places. 'د.ل.‏ 20,000' is twenty dinars, not twenty thousand. Any scraper reading these as integers will overstate Libyan medicine prices by 1000x.

Country-of-manufacture and anti-counterfeit markers are part of the product name in Libyan listings, because parallel imports of the same brand differ in price: 'بنادول شراب للحرارة للاطفال الاصلي الفرنسي' vs 'البنادول الاصلي صناعة انجليزية'. dsm.ly does the same in English: '(UK BOOK)', '(Australia)', '(FRANCE-TUN)', 'ALFA' (the local importer).

dialect.gloss: Amoxil / co-amoxiclav — Arabic spellings of the amoxicillin brands
dialect.note: Amoxil is spelled BOTH اومكسيل and اموكسيل in Libyan pharmacy copy; the اومكسيل variant is the one that appears on actual price lists and is missing from most transliteration tables. Augmentin is اوجمنتين and is glossed by Libyan pharmacists as أموكسيكلاف.

dialect.gloss: the mg/5ml strength used as the product identifier
dialect.note: Libyan antibiotic-syrup listings identify the product by bare strength number with no unit: 'اوجمنتين شراب 156', 'اومكسيل شراب 125-250', 'اوجمنتين شراب ٦٠٠'. The number is the whole SKU. Arabic-Indic digits (٦٠٠، ٤٥٧) appear alongside Western ones, sometimes in the same post.

dialect.gloss: Sitamol / Cetamol — a Tunisian-made paracetamol syrup
dialect.note: A cheap Tunisian-manufactured paracetamol syrup sold in Libya as 'شراب سيتامول', distinct from Panadol/Adol. Libyan pharmacists contrast it with بنادول by concentration ('السيتال شراب تركيز 250 مجم'). Related local names seen in the same market: بارالفيت Paralvit, دوليبران Doliprane, بروفيمول Brufemol.

Libyan container word used for BOTH a 400 g milk-powder tin and a small evaporated-milk can — it carries no size and no infant/adult signal. Seen as 'حليب دانا حكه كبيره', 'حليب المعمورة حكه كبيره', '16 دينار الحكه 400جرام'. A matcher must not treat 'حكة حليب' as evidence of infant formula.

The wholesale unit above the carton: 'سعر اللّتر الواحد 2.5 دينار الاستيــكة 30' = 2.5 LYD per 1 L carton, 30 LYD for the shrink-pack (12). Also used for eggs ('استيكة دحي'). Prices quoted per استيكة must never be recorded as unit prices.
The standard Libyan retail label for drinking UHT milk; the official price bulletin uses 'حليب معقم … لتر'. This is the token that positively marks uht_milk_1l.
A separate line item from معقم in Libyan price bulletins and pricing decrees, and cheaper. NOT uht_milk_1l.
Sold in 170 ml cans by the same brands that sell UHT litres (الزهرات, جودي). Neither drinking milk nor formula. Distinct from 'حليب مكثف محلى' (sweetened condensed).
Attaches to Nido ('حليب نيدو المقوي', 'حليبي المقوي') — a DRINKING milk powder. Fortification language is not evidence of infant formula.

The single most reliable infant-formula marker in Libyan shop text. Appears with no 'رضع' or 'اطفال' token at all: 'حليب نستوجين … رقم 1 … رقم 2', 'بريمالاك 3', 'حليب اطفال الماني رقم 3'. Stage 2 and 3 are still infant formula for Qeema's purposes.
Unambiguous. 'حليب للرضع', 'غذاء حليب مكمل للرضع', 'تركيبة للرضع'. Contrast with 'اطفال', which is ambiguous (see disambiguation).

Pharmacy shelf category covering AR (anti-reflux), CMA (cow's-milk allergy), amino-acid formulas: 'لينالاك AR للارتجاع', 'برميلاك CMA', 'الفامينو'. Still infant formula but priced far above the 400 g standard tin (comments cite 100+ LYD) — must not be averaged into infant_formula_400g.
A local (non-Nestlé) infant/toddler cereal-type food, e.g. 'لحوس الامين' from لبدة للصناعات الغذائية. A plausible baby_cereal_400g sibling but sold in different pack sizes — flagged, not labelled.
The bulletin writes '6.75 دل'; e-commerce writes '45.00 د.ل'. Both are LYD. Beware: '16,000 دينار' / '2,000د.ع' in the same Arabic search space are Iraqi dinar, not Libyan.

Libya has run subsidised infant-formula distribution through designated pharmacies; subsidised prices sit far below market and should never be merged with retail. (2024 scheme: 13–26 LYD across 82 pharmacies.)

This is THE Libyan word. Every 2026 Libyan price survey and every Libyan stationery storefront uses كراسة for the everyday school notebook; none of them uses دفتر for it. The masculine singular كراس is equally current ('دستة الكراس المدرسي', 'مصانع الكراس المحلية'). Price band 0.50–4.0 LYD by page count and quality.

dialect.gloss: a bundle/dozen of exercise books — the normal Libyan retail unit
dialect.note: Critically NOT always 12. Observed as 10 ('دستة 10 كراسات 9دينار'), and quoted at 7, 9, 10 and 15 LYD across shops and years. Families buy by the دستة, not singly, so any per-unit cost model must divide by the stated count, never assume 12.

dialect.gloss: the plastic jacket or cover slipped over a كراسة
dialect.note: A separate purchase, not the notebook. 'سفار كراسه ب 2 دينار' — a cover can cost as much as the notebook it covers. مكتبة السفير lists a whole category 'أسفار تغليف'. Must be a hard negative for school_notebook_80p.

dialect.gloss: biro, ballpoint pen (from the brand Biro)
dialect.note: Libyan colloquial for a cheap ballpoint. Seen advertised at 20 قرش (0.20 LYD) alongside 'كراسة 60 ورقة 1.25'. A likely miss for the catalogue — it does not look like قلم at all.

dialect.gloss: ballpoint ('dry' pen), as opposed to gel, fountain or felt
dialect.note: جاف is an ADJECTIVE on قلم حبر, not a noun. Full form 'قلم الحبر الجاف'. Libyan shops use قلم جاف and قلم حبر interchangeably for the same product; المسار's survey word is 'قلم الحبر المدرسي'.
riad.ly files it in the same category name as pens: 'أقلام الحبر والكركت'. It is NOT a writing pen — hard negative for ballpoint_pen.
The Libyan plural مباري appears in the national price survey: 'وبالنسبة إلى مباري أقلام الرصاص، تراوحت أسعار الأنواع العادية بين 0.250 ودينار واحد'. Distractor.

dialect.gloss: eraser — both words in live Libyan use
dialect.note: استيكة is the colloquial, محاية the shop-catalogue word ('محاية ممتازة 2B لا تثرك أثر'). Distractor.
شنطة (colloquial) and حقيبة (formal) are both fully Libyan and interchangeable for a school backpack. riad.ly's own category is 'الحقائب والشناطي', using both.

dialect.gloss: school bag — but NOT Libyan usage
dialect.note: Searching محفظة مدرسية + ليبيا returned almost entirely Algerian (prices in دج/3900da), Moroccan (مراكش) and Iraqi (٦ الاف) sellers. In Libya محفظة means a wallet. Treating محفظة مدرسية as a Libyan school_backpack wording risks importing Maghrebi listings and their currencies.

Every كشكول + ليبيا hit was Egyptian (priced in جنيه: 'الباكو اتناشر كشكول بمية تسعة وتسعين جنيه'), Iraqi (مكتبة كشكول في بغداد), or a book title/place name. Zero Libyan retail use for an exercise book. Should not be a Libyan wording for school_notebook_80p.

dialect.gloss: used loosely for any sub-dinar amount
dialect.note: Libyan sellers write '0.50 قرش', '0.75 قرش', '20 قرش', '١.٤٩ قرش' meaning 0.50 / 0.75 / 0.20 / 1.49 LYD. The word does not mean 1/100 here — it is a filler for 'and change'. Parsing '1.49 قرش' as 0.0149 LYD would be a costing error.
In Libya مكتبة is the ordinary word for the shop that sells كراسات and أقلام — مكتبة الخطوة الأولى, مكتبة المهندس, مكتبة السفير. قرطاسية is the synonym. Both name shops, not products.
Distractor for school_backpack — frequently bundled with bags ('حقيبة فنون درجة أولى مع مقلمة').

dialect.gloss: stapled / sewn binding of a كراسة
dialect.note: The Libyan quality axis for exercise books. 'كراس 60 ورقة دبوس' (stapled, cheapest) vs 'كراسة 100 ورقة الحجم..B4 الكبير خياطة..وليس دبوس' (sewn, dearer). Binding plus page count explains most of the price spread inside كراسة.

The ordinary everyday Libyan word for eggs, used across Tripoli, Benghazi, Sirte, Misrata, Zliten, Sabha and Zawiya in the pages seen. Shops, news pages and government-price commentary all use it — this is not slang, it is the default. Also spelled with the definite article as الدحي, and occasionally الدحى with alif maqsura. بيض is understood but reads as formal/MSA; many posts write both, e.g. 'بيض ليبي "دحي"' and 'طبق البيض "الدحي"'.
Singulative of دحي. Seen as '30 دحيه' for a tray count and 'تكلفة الدحية الوحدة' for unit cost.

dialect.gloss: the egg tray / flat (the moulded pack of 30)
dialect.note: THIS IS THE PEN BUG. استيكة in Egyptian and Levantine Arabic means an eraser/rubber, which is why 'دحي الاستيكة' was matched to a ballpoint pen. In Libyan it is the flat pulp tray, and it is fully interchangeable with طبق: 'الطبق (الاستيكة)', 'استيكة دحي السعر 10 دينار', 'اخر سعر استيكة الدحي كم وصلت'. It also generalises to other tray-packed produce — 'استيكة الطماطم' is a flat of tomatoes — so the disambiguator has to be the following noun, not استيكة itself.

dialect.gloss: tray of eggs; the standard retail unit
dialect.note: The most common way a price is quoted: 'سعر الطبق 12 دينار'. The count is usually left implicit — the Libyan طبق is 30. When a count is written it comes as a bare numeral, e.g. 'طبق فيه 30طرف' or 'طبق دحي سمان 30 دحيه'. Fractions occur: 'طبق ونص'. Plural طبقين = two trays.

dialect.gloss: piece, unit — the counter used for individual eggs
dialect.note: 'طبق فيه 30طرف' = a tray containing 30 pieces. This is how pack count actually gets written when it gets written at all.

Real, but ambiguous in practice: most hits are the EMPTY carton reused for crafts or as a rough measure in catering ads, not an egg sale. Treat as weak evidence for eggs_30 unless a price accompanies it.
The wholesale tier. At 165 LYD on 2026-08-15 while a retail tray was 15 LYD, so it is roughly a dozen trays — but the count is not printed and must never be inferred into a per-tray figure.

A distinct, dearer grade — advertised as 'خالي من علفه وخالي من حظائر' (no feed, no cages) at 20–23 LYD a tray while cage eggs were 12. Same pack, different product tier. Also دحي بلدي and دحي وطني (domestic Libyan, as opposed to imported).
Distractor. Sold in trays of 30 exactly like hen eggs and at a similar-looking number (15 LYD), so it will match on shape. Per the brief these are not eggs_30.

The clearest signal that a tray is NOT food. Breeder trays — دحي براهما, دحي رومي, دحي براهمي زهري — are advertised as مخصب and priced 20–24 LYD, right in the table-egg range. مخصب or a breed name should veto eggs_30.

The trade/official register — used by the producers' union (شعبة بيض المائدة) and ministry reporting, not by shoppers. Also بيض مغلف = packaged eggs, which carried a premium (30 LYD vs 25 for loose in one report).

The single biggest trap on chicken. The daily Tripoli boards quote الدجاج الحي per kg (14 LYD on 2026-08-13) and الدجاج المدبوح بدون أحشاء separately (~19.40–19.50 wholesale the same week). They are not the same kilo. مدبوح is Libyan for slaughtered; بدون أحشاء = without offal.

dialect.gloss: broiler chicken — BUT also a fish name in Libyan seafood trade
dialect.note: Hard negative. On Tripoli fish-shop pages فروج appears in lists beside مناني، جغالي، شولة، رقيد، حوت, all fish/seafood. A rule that maps فروج → chicken will misfire on every seafood post. حوت = fish generally in Libyan, not whale.
Cut drives a 2x spread on the same day at the same shop: thighs and wings 15 LYD/kg, breast 30 LYD/kg (Benghazi, 2026-07-28). Any single stored chicken_1kg number is really a cut choice in disguise.
Offal, explicit distractors. Note liver at 35 LYD/kg was dearer than breast at 30 on the same board, so price plausibility will not catch this — only the word will.
طازة is the colloquial form of طازج. مبرد (chilled) and مجمد (frozen) are contrasted explicitly and repeatedly in ads — 'مبرد ليس مجمد' — because frozen is the cheap tier.
Imported frozen birds are priced PER BIRD by gram band (1000/1100/1200/1300/1400/1600), never per kg — e.g. 'دجاج برازيلي الوزن 1100 السعر 9 دينار'. Only fresh domestic chicken is sold per kilo.

تن is what shops actually write ('تن الجيد', 'تن السفينة', 'تن وادي الكوف', 'تن بيتي', 'تن امريكانا', 'تن المضياف', 'تن الصفوة'); تونة is the fuller/formal form and is what news and consumers write. Both are common. علبة and عبوة both mean the tin/pack.

All four spellings occur in the wild, including bare Latin '185g'. The neighbouring sizes on the same shelves are 65, 140, 160, 180, 200, 400, 900 and 1700 g — 180 g in particular is a near-miss that must not collapse into 185. Decimal prices are written with either a dot or a comma (2.75 / 2,75).

dialect.gloss: in olive oil vs in vegetable oil
dialect.note: The same 185 g tin carries two prices depending on the oil (2.75 vs 2.50 in one shop list). The oil is part of the pack spec, not a garnish.
Transliterated species grade that appears in tuna branding (تن يلوفن وادي الكوف, تونة الوفاء نوع اليلوفين).

dialect.gloss: 'burn' price = a deep discount; كزيوني = knockout/bargain (Libyan slang)
dialect.note: Ubiquitous in offer posts ('سعر حرق 20دينار', 'بسعر كزيووووني', 'كتيبة حرق الأسعار'). Signals a promotional price, not a normal shelf price — worth flagging rather than treating as the going rate.

dialect.gloss: the standard Libyan household drinking-water bottle, 5–7 litres; also spelled بانقا / بانقه
dialect.note: Libya Al-Ahrar glosses it explicitly: 'عبوة الـ 7 لترات أو ما يعرف بالـ بانقة'. A Libyan machinery dealer advertises a 'خط تعبئه مياه الشرب حجم 5 -7 لتر بسعر انتاجيه 2000 بانقه بالساعه', confirming the word spans 5L and 7L, so بانقة alone does NOT pin the size to 7L. Not a Facebook-only coinage — it is the ordinary retail word.

dialect.gloss: a dozen — the standard selling unit for 0.5L bottles (12 عبوة)
dialect.note: Almost every 2026 Libyan water price headline quotes the دستة, not the بانقة. A دستة price (7–10 LYD) looks similar in magnitude to a بانقة price (3–5 LYD) and is easy to mis-assign — this is the single biggest confusion risk for drinking_water_7l.

dialect.gloss: container / pack — generic, always qualified by size (عبوة 7 لتر، عبوة نصف لتر، عبوة 300 ملي)
dialect.note: The most common neutral head-word in news copy. Never size-bearing on its own.

dialect.gloss: bottle — used for the 7L water bottle especially in the south (Ubari/Sabha) and in TV captions
dialect.note: 'الخمس دنانير لقنينة 7 لتر' (Ubari). Used without a size just as often, in which case it is unsafe to map to the 7L item.

dialect.gloss: bottle — but in Libyan usage قارورة الغاز also means a gas cylinder
dialect.note: IMPORTANT CROSS-ITEM TRAP: 'قارورة ماء' is a water bottle while 'قارورة غاز' is a cooking-gas cylinder. Any matcher keying on قارورة alone will cross-wire drinking_water_7l and cooking_gas_11kg. Also note 'فرشاة تنظيف قارورة الماء' (bottle-cleaning brush, 55 LYD) is a hard negative.

Brega's own wording encodes the weight in the colour: 'سعر أسطوانة الغاز الزرقاء، حجم 15 كجم (( 2 )) دينار' / 'سعر أسطوانة الغاز الصفراء، حجم 11 كجم ((1.50)) دينار'. So a post saying only 'الصفراء' is still specifying the 11kg item.

dialect.gloss: gas cylinder (Egyptian-flavoured term, used in pan-Arab TV coverage of Libya)
dialect.note: 'أنابيب غاز الطهي ... خمسين دينارا للانبوبة الواحدة'. Appears alongside أسطوانة in the same reports; worth carrying as a synonym.

dialect.gloss: fibreglass (composite) gas cylinder, the lightweight import type
dialect.note: Distinct product from the steel 11kg cylinder; appears in supply-crisis discussion.

dialect.gloss: Brega 'immediate-fill point' — the official outlet where the subsidised refill price applies
dialect.note: The phrase is the reliable marker that a quoted gas price is the official/subsidised one rather than the street one.

dialect.gloss: refundable financial guarantee / deposit on a gas cylinder — 240 LYD in 2026, raised from 50 LYD
dialect.note: NOT a price. It is the largest gas-related number a Libyan sees in 2026 and is routinely mistaken for one; the news copy has to say so explicitly ('لا يُعتبر سعر بيع').

dialect.gloss: water tanker truck / tank load — sold by the barrel or by the 12,000-litre load
dialect.note: Tobruk's municipal tariff (26 Mar 2026): 85 LYD for a 55–60 barrel (12,000L) tanker; other reports put a خزان at 120–140 LYD and up to 200 LYD. Entirely separate market from bottled water — a strong hard negative in the hundreds-of-dinars range.

dialect.gloss: 1/1000 of a dinar in colloquial price talk — '75 قرشاً لنصف لتر'
dialect.note: Sub-dinar water prices are quoted in قروش, and in writing as 0.750 دينار. A parser must treat '75 قرش' and '0.750 دينار' as the same figure.

dialect.gloss: the wooden/plastic crate that fresh vegetables are sold in; for tomatoes it holds roughly 10–28 kg depending on the crate
dialect.note: STRONGEST FRESH SIGNAL FOUND. Used only of fresh produce, never of a tin. A vendor states it outright: 'قابية الطماطم هادي فيها خمسة وعشرين كيلو الى ثمانية وعشرين كيلو'. Also spelled قابيه / القابيا. Any string containing قابية is fresh with very high confidence.
Paste signal. 'معجون طماطم بنكهة أصلية قوطية بوزن 800 غم'. Pairs with كارتون for the case.

dialect.gloss: a shrink-wrapped tray/sleeve of tins, normally 12 or 24
dialect.note: Paste signal — a retail multipack unit that only exists for canned goods. 'سعر العلبة: 1.5 دينار فقط الستيكة (12 علبة): 17 دينار'. Never used of fresh produce.

AMBIGUOUS — DO NOT USE AS A DISAMBIGUATOR. Used for a case of paste tins ('كرتونة (صندوق معجون الطماطم) المكونة من 24 علبة سعة 400 غرام') AND for the 25 kg wholesale crate of fresh tomatoes ('95 دينارًا للصندوق (25 كغم)'). Only the accompanying number disambiguates it.

dialect.gloss: sauce; in Libya used as a straight synonym for tomato paste
dialect.note: Paste, never fresh. A Libyan recipe writes the gloss explicitly: 'معجون طماطم (صلصة)'. Compound 'معجون صلصة الطماطم' also occurs. CAVEAT: bare صلصة is not uniquely tomato — 'الهريسة الليبية هي صلصة حارة' uses it of harissa. So صلصة طماطم = paste; صلصة alone = paste or harissa, but never fresh tomatoes.
The unambiguous paste word. 'معجون طماطم' / 'معجون الطماطم' is the standard commercial and official term (used by the Ministry of Economy and the Price Stabilisation Fund).
Paste signal. Concentration percentage is printed on paste tins and appears in ad copy: 'صلصة طماطم أرابيلا جودة مميزة وتركيز عالٍ 28–30%'.
All paste-side multipack units. 'سعر القطعة 2.50 دينار سعر الدسته 30 دينار'.

NEGATIVE FINDING — this is NOT the Libyan form. Every search hit for طماطة returned Iraqi and Gulf pages (prices in دينار عراقي, ريال, Mosul/Kirkuk/Karbala). Libyan sources use طماطم exclusively, occasionally طماط. Including طماطة in a Libyan matcher would import Iraqi noise.
NEGATIVE FINDING — zero Libyan hits. Not Libyan usage.
Appears in Libyan brand copy: 'طماط No.1'. Worth matching as a variant.

THREE-WAY POLYSEMY. (1) the chilli paste — 'معجون فلفل أحمر حار'; (2) in the Levant/Jordan a semolina sweet — 'هريسة المنجد ... كعك معاني... حلبة'; (3) apparently the fresh hot pepper itself in Libyan vegetable price lists, where هريسة is priced per unit alongside كوسا and باذنجان. Only (1) is harissa_can.

dialect.gloss: 'Arab harissa' — the traditional home-made Libyan harissa
dialect.note: Common synonym in Libyan usage, distinguishing home/traditional harissa from the imported tinned kind. 'متوفر هريسه عربيه منشوره في الشمس وفيها تومه' (sun-dried, with garlic). Related synonyms: دبس الفليفلة, شطة.

Sold loose alongside fresh produce in Libyan buy/sell listings, priced at 10 dinars in the same list as 'طماطم درجة اولى 4 كيلو'. This is the domestic artisanal form, not a branded tin — evidence that Libyan harissa circulates outside the packaged-goods channel.

Functions as a paste signal in Libya. Fresh tomatoes sold in Libya are local (جالو، درنة) or Egyptian; tinned paste is overwhelmingly Italian-imported or made to Italian spec. So 'طماطم إيطالية .. 400 جــرام' and 'طماطم غـالـيـة إطالي' both mean paste.
Fresh signal — Libyan growing-region origin markers, used only of fresh produce.
Fresh signal — the official Libya Trade Network bulletin grades fresh tomatoes and prices the two grades separately (7 vs 4 LYD/kg on 2026-07-09). Paste is never graded this way.

FALSE FRIEND / HARD NEGATIVE. 'ليبي' here is the brand Libby's (ليبيز), not the nationality adjective 'Libyan'. A naive matcher keying on ليبي + طماطم will pull in Gulf ketchup listings. Confirmed by the retailer's own brand field: 'العلامة التجارية: ليبيز'.
Libyan sales slang, endlessly elongated with repeated waws. Appears in almost every promo post from western-Libyan grocery pages. A tokeniser that does not collapse repeated letters will miss it.
Price-promo intensifier, not a product word.
Standard opener for a stock-arrival post; the product name follows immediately, so it is a useful anchor for extraction.
Libyan/Tunisian form. Coexists with مكرونة (bulletins, shop pages), معكرونة (MSA), مكرونه/مقرونه (final ه). All four must map to pasta.
Used interchangeably with دقيق and طحين. Attaches to any size — 'شكارة دقيق الصفوة فارينة 5 كيلو'. Carries NO size information at all.

dialect.term: دقيق الأغراض المنزلية vs دقيق المخابز
dialect.note: THE reliable distinguisher for the flour problem. Official Libyan bulletins always price 'الأغراض المنزلية' per كيلو جرام and 'المخابز' per قنطار. If a string carries المنزلية → wheat_flour_1kg; if it carries المخابز → the bulk item.
Grade words appear on BOTH sizes — 'دقيق ليبي فاخر شكارة 50 كيلو' and 'دقيق الأغراض المنزلية الفاخر 1 كيلو جرام'. Grade is NOT a size signal. Note الصفوة and الريحان are also brand names.

dialect.gloss: a Libyan flour grade (coarser bread flour)
dialect.note: TRAP: reads like 'the quarter'. In both bulletins it sits alongside الناعم and السميد as a grade, priced per kilo and per قنطار. Do not parse as a quantity.
Sold both as دقيق الأغراض المنزلية (السميد) at 1 kg and as دقيق المخابز (السميد) by the قنطار. It is its own product — should not collapse into wheat_flour_1kg.

dialect.term: حبة طويلة / حبة قصيرة / حبه مكركبه
dialect.gloss: long grain / short grain / clumpy-round grain
dialect.note: Rice descriptors. All are rice_1kg when a kilo is named. 'مكركبة' is distinctively Libyan.
Couscous descriptors. 'مبروشة' (from برش, to grate) marks artisanal couscous and commands a much higher kilo price (9.50 vs 4).

dialect.gloss: a pasta shape name in Libyan pasta catalogues
dialect.note: TRAP: لوبيا normally means black-eyed beans. In 'مكرونة محلية (لوبيا) 400 جرام' it is the cut/shape. Context word مكرونة must win.
Two spellings for the same brand, both meaning long-grain rice. Not a person.
'كيلو سكر 250 درهم (0.25 دينار)'. Appears mainly in nostalgia posts. If read as a modern dirham the figure is wrong by orders of magnitude.

dialect.gloss: piastre; also used loosely for a small sum
dialect.note: 'سعر الشكارة الواحدة 75 قرش' for empty sacks. Also appears as a Tunisian-dinar subunit in cross-border price comparisons.
'دل' with no dots is very common in shop posts. Also seen glued to the number: '15دينار', '26دينار', '3,250دينار'.
Libyan. 'توا وقته' = 'now is its season'. Marks a post as current, useful as a freshness hint.
Three price tiers that appear in the same post. 'سعر القطاعي' is the retail column in official bulletins. A scraper that grabs the جملة الجملة figure and labels it retail will under-report.
Doubles the price of sugar (3.25 vs 5.00) and rice at identical pack sizes. Should be preserved as a variant axis, not averaged away.

dialect.gloss: Libyan dishes made from flour, pasta or rice
dialect.note: DISTRACTOR class. 'رشدة دقيق فارينة' is a noodle dish, not a flour product. Recipe posts mention 'نص كيلو' and product names but sell nothing.
Quality claim on home-produced couscous sold by the kilo.

disambiguation.observation: A stage number is the disambiguator that actually works. Libyan sellers routinely write 'حليب <brand> رقم N' with no 'رضع' and no 'اطفال' anywhere in the string. If a matcher learns 'حليب + brand + رقم 1|2|3' it resolves the majority of formula listings without needing an infant token.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب نستوجين صناعة فرنسية رقم 1 غذاء حليب للرضع رقم 2 غذاء حليب مكمل للرضع

disambiguation.observation: The second reliable disambiguator is an explicit age band inside the product title — Libyan e-commerce titles carry it even when the brand alone would be ambiguous.
disambiguation.evidence: Primalac، رقم 1 لعمر من 0 - 6 شهور، مدعم بالحديد 400ج

disambiguation.observation: 'اطفال' is NOT a disambiguator. Libyan shops label Nido — a general drinking milk powder — as 'حليب اطفال', in 300 g, 400 g and 1800 g tins. So 'حليب اطفال <brand>' can be either side of the confusion; only 'رضع' is safe.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب اطفال نيدو 1800 جرام السعر 86 دينار

disambiguation.observation: Same page, same brand, explicitly aged 1–3 years: this is growing-up/drinking milk being sold under the 'حليب الاطفال' banner. A pattern-matcher keying on 'حليب الاطفال' would price a 15 LYD milk powder as a 32 LYD formula tin.
disambiguation.evidence: توفرت كمية جديدة من حليب الاطفال نيدو للاطفال من عمر 1 سنة الى 3 سنوات … السعر السابق 19.500 ❌

disambiguation.observation: Pack size does not disambiguate either. Plain full-fat drinking milk powder is sold in Libya in the SAME 400 g tin as infant formula, at roughly a third of the price (10–16 LYD vs ~28–45 LYD). Any rule of the form 'حليب + 400 جرام → infant_formula_400g' is wrong.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب بودرة اورين ٤٠٠ جرام أقل سعر : 15 دينار

disambiguation.observation: Second instance of the same 400 g drinking-powder trap, from a different city (Benghazi, السلماني الشرقي), at 10 LYD.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب بودرة ✨ اورين ✨ 400 جرام السعر 10 دينار

disambiguation.observation: Third instance, a Tripoli own-brand: a 400 g tin described only as 'حليب بودرة درجة أولى كامل الدسم عبوة العلبة 400 جرام'. 'كامل الدسم' is the token that saves it — full-fat is a drinking-milk descriptor and never appears on infant formula.
disambiguation.evidence: HALEBONA حليب بودرة درجة أولى كامل الدسم عبوة العلبة 400 جرام المكان. طرابلس

disambiguation.observation: Positive markers for drinking milk on the liquid side: 'معقم' (UHT) and 'لتر'. The official Libyan bulletin uses exactly this form, so 'حليب معقم <brand>' → uht_milk_1l is safe, and 'حليب مبستر' (pasteurised) and 'حليب مركز' (evaporated, 170 ml) are safe negatives.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب معقم جودي | لتر | 6.75 دل … حليب مركز جودي | 170 مل | 3 دل

disambiguation.observation: BRANDS THAT SELL BOTH SIDES — Nestlé is the worst offender: نيدو (drinking milk powder, also marketed for 1–3 year olds) vs نان / نستوجين (infant formula) vs سيريلاك (baby cereal). A bare 'حليب نستله' string is unresolvable.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب الاطفال نستوجين من نستلة … نحن نهتم بطفلك متوفر في صيدليات و أسواق ليبيا

disambiguation.observation: BRANDS THAT SELL BOTH SIDES — the Libyan dairy houses جودي، النسيم، الجيد، الزهرات، الريحان each sell 'حليب معقم' by the litre AND 'حليب مركز' by the 170 ml can under one brand name, so brand alone never fixes the product; the qualifier (معقم / مركز / مبستر) does.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب معقم الزهرات | لتر | 7 دل … حليب مركز الزهرات | 170 مل | 3.25 دل

disambiguation.observation: BRANDS THAT SELL BOTH SIDES — دانا (Dana) sells UHT litres ('حليب دانا كامل الدسم 1 لتر') and a canned product referred to only as 'حليب دانا حكه كبيره'. The word حكة supplies a container but not a category.
disambiguation.evidence: حليب دانا كامل الدسم 1 لتر 🔴سعر القطعة 2.5 دينار 🔴سعر الصندوق 29 دينار

disambiguation.observation: Libyan formula brand gazetteer worth adding to the catalogue, all seen on Libyan seller/pharmacy pages: بريمالاك Primalac (incl. Premium and CMA), بيبيلاك Bebelac, نستوجين Nestogen, نان NAN (incl. Comfort), ابتاميل Aptamil, إس 26 / S-26, SMA, سيليا Celia (Newtsern), ليبتوميل Laptomil, بيدياميل Pediamil, الديلاك Delac, هيرو بيبي Hero Baby, نوفالاك Novalac, نيورالاك Neuralac, فيتالي Vitaly, لينالاك Linalac AR, الفامينو Alfamino.
disambiguation.evidence: شركة فارماليس ليبيا تعلن عن وصول حليب بريمالاك بـ جميع الأرقام

disambiguation.observation: Cross-currency trap in the same Arabic search space: 'حليب الأطفال … بسعر 2,000د.ع' and '16,000 دينار' are Iraqi dinar listings that surface on identical queries. Any harvested formula price must be checked for a Libyan seller before the number is trusted.
disambiguation.evidence: سيريلاك قمح من 6 اشهر سعر 2,000د.ع

The brand owner's own page titles the product video '#غالية نشارك معكم مراحل تصنيع معجون الطماطم من غالية في افضل المصانع الإيطالية' — 'we show you the stages of manufacturing TOMATO PASTE from Ghalia in the best Italian factories'. A distributor's copy for the same product reads 'طماطم #غاليه من المعمورة ... مصنوعة وفق معايير ايطالية مع اختيار طماطم ذات جودة عالية لانتاج معجون'. Owner is شركة المعمورة لاستيراد المواد الغذائية, described on its own page as 'واحدة من أكبر شركات تصنيع المواد الغذائية في ليبيا'. Retail listing 'طماطم غـالـيـة إطالي' at Mecca Mall confirms it is sold as an Italian tinned line. RESOLVED: any 'طماطم غالية' string is tomato paste, never fresh.

disambiguation.brand: غالية — the ordinary adjective, NOT a brand
disambiguation.evidence: CRITICAL TRAP, and the reason this string family is so hard. غالية is also the everyday Arabic feminine adjective 'expensive'. Public comment threads about food inflation are full of the bare sentence 'الطماطم غاليه' meaning 'tomatoes are expensive': 'والله ما فاهمين ... الطماطم غاليه في كل مكان في العالم'; 'حتى مصر طماطم غاليه'; 'حبيبي الطماطم غالية في العالم كلو'. So 'طماطم غالية' is THREE-WAY ambiguous: (a) the paste brand, (b) fresh tomatoes described as expensive, (c) a bare complaint about prices that is not a product mention at all. Disambiguator that works: the brand reading is nearly always written with the hashtag (#غاليه / #غالية), with 'إيطالي', or with a seller/mall name; the adjective reading appears in a full sentence with a verb or a place ('في كل مكان', 'حتى مصر'). Sense (c) should be excluded from the catalogue entirely.

Retail ad uses the bare-brand form and the tin spec in the same breath: 'طماطم علبة وزن400جرام سعرالعلبة2.50دينار' under the hashtag #طماطم_الجيد_أقل_سعر. The importer's own announcement: 'تعــلن شركة الجيد لإستيراد المواد الغذائية عن وصول ... سعر بيع صنف معجون طماطم الجيد للمستهلك 2.5 دينار'. A wholesale list prices 'طماطم الجيد(12 علبة) :24 د. ل'. RESOLVED: paste.

شركة الرضا للصناعات الغذائية makes BOTH a tomato line and a harissa line, and the shop post makes the sequence explicit: 'هريسة الفلفل الأحمر من رضا / أنتاج ليبي : بعد #طماطم 🍅 #الرضا جديد ... #هريسة 🌶 #الرضا'. i.e. 'after Al-Rida tomato, new: Al-Rida harissa'. The 'طماطم الرضا' being referenced is a manufactured packaged line (a food-industries company launching a product), not fresh produce. Post is a business page (سوق إعليوة للتسوق, Zliten), dated 23 December 2024. NOTE: the harissa is 'صناعة ليبية بالكامل و يستعملوا في الفلفل من المزارع الليبية' — a genuinely Libyan-made harissa.
Appears under the explicit header 'طماطم معجون' in a Tripoli Mall wholesale list: 'طماطم صاحب الجبل (24 علبة) :69 د. ل'. The unit '(24 علبة)' is a case of tins.
Same list, same 'طماطم معجون' header: 'طماطم ميجور(24 علبة) :48 د. ل'.
Same list: 'طماطم بلدنا(12 علبة) :23 د. ل'.

Same list: 'طماطم الاميرة(24 علبة):48 د. ل' and 'طماطم الاميرة(12 علبة):24 د. ل'. CAUTION: 'هريسة الأميرة' is separately a Libyan-style harissa brand sold in Egypt (wa7et-siwa.com), so الأميرة alone does not fix the product — it fixes the form only in combination with طماطم or هريسة.
Same list: 'طماطم باكنا(12 علبة) : 21 د. ل'.
'معجون طماطم "الزهرات" (حلال) الوزن: 400 غرام للعلبة' and separately 'متوفر الآن معجون طماطم "الزهرات".. منتج إيطالي طعم إيطالي أصيل'. Exactly the 400g tin the catalogue item describes.
Importer announcement: 'تعلن شركة الواحات المتجددة لاستيراد المواد الغذائية عن توفر كميات من معجون الطماطم "القبطان"، إيطالي الصنع، بسعر بيع للمستهلك 1 دينار ليبي'.
'معجون طماطم الطيبات من المنتجات المميزة لدينا ... يصنف من أفضل منتجات معجون الطماطم لدى الأسوق في ليبيا'.
'ملعقة وحدة من معجون🍅طماطم #لمتنا تغير طعم الطبخة كاملة' — 'one spoonful of Lamtna tomato paste'. Sold by the قطعة (2.50 LYD) and by the دسته (30 LYD).

شركة أصيل announced 'قريباً 🇱🇾 مصنع معجون طماطم' — a tomato paste factory. Brand copy elsewhere pairs 'طماطم أصيل' with 'صلصة طماطم غنية بلونها، نكهتها، وجودتها'. The bare string 'طماطم أصيل' is therefore paste, but only resolvable via the brand.

Market page: 'كيف وصل كميه من طماطم السلدور طماطم الرقم 1 في سوق الليبي ... متوفر داخل ميرا ماركت', with 'طماطم معجون ايطالي بسعر' in the same page's related copy. Confidence: good, not absolute — the co-occurrence is on the page rather than inside the one sentence.
'معجون عزيز معجون طماطم بنكهة أصلية قوطية بوزن 800 غم السعر: (( 1.750 دينار )) سعر الكارتون 12 قوطية'. Note the 800g tin — a real pack size alongside the 400g one.
'وصل حديثًا صلصة طماطم أرابيلا جودة مميزة وتركيز عالٍ 28–30% ✨ العبوة الصغيرة المميزة 70 غم'. A 70g single-use tin — another pack size to expect.
Product label reproduced in the ad: 'altunsa معجون طماطم DOMATES SALÇASI / TOMATO PASTE'. Turkish import, distributed in Tripoli ('واخيرا العرض وصل لي العاصمة الحبيبة طرابلس').
'عرض خاص وجديد معجون طماطم البستان نوعية محلية جديدة بوزن ...' — note 'نوعية محلية', a locally-produced paste.
'طماطم نابولي 400 جرام' listed in the same ad as 'صلصة طماطم' copy — the 400g tin.
'طماط No.1 .. الجودة المضمونة لطبخاتك اللذيذة' with the page's own text 'على بركة الله تم وصول معجون ... وسعر العلبة' — arriving stock of معجون sold by the علبة.
'Jana Rosa معجون الطماطم الغداء الليبي اجود المنتجات بمعايير عالمية' with a Libyan +218 sales number.
Aldaaysi Markets: 'معجون الطماطم من علامة توسان'.

Appears twice as 'ستيكة طماطم حكة' and 'الحكية 1.5 دينار'. The unit ستيكة puts it firmly on the paste side, but I could not open a page where the brand name and the word معجون appear together, so I am not asserting the brand attribution. Recorded as unresolved rather than guessed.

A real Libyan cannery — its own product labels read 'بلد المنشأ: ليبيا/الزاوية (Libya/Al-Zawiya)'. Its harissa copy: 'وصفة ليبية أصلية ✓ فلفل حار طبيعي 100% ✓ نكهة غنية وعميقة ✓ مثالية للطهي والتغميس ✓ الوزن الصافي: 185 غرام'. This is the clearest evidence found that a packaged Libyan harissa SKU exists at all — 185g, not the 380g/400g the catalogue might assume.

Tunisian harissa brand, the reference product in Libya: 'عندنا في ليبيا هريسة الوطن القبلي علبة الكبيرة ٥دينار'. The comparison brand كوجينا (Cucina) appears in the same thread but priced in UAE dirhams, so it is not a Libyan retail datum.
Libyan market-watch TikTok discusses 'هريسة الحطاب' and whether its price matches its quality. Form is clear (harissa); I did not open a page giving pack or price.

HARD NEGATIVE, not a tomato-paste or fresh brand. 'كاتشب طماطم ليبي 760 جم' is Libby's KETCHUP; the retailer's brand field says 'العلامة التجارية: ليبيز'. Any rule that reads ليبي as 'Libyan' next to طماطم will mislabel Gulf ketchup listings as Libyan tomato products.

The canonical example of the problem is a Tripoli Mall wholesale list headed 'طماطم معجون ❤️' and then itemised as 'طماطم صاحب الجبل (24 علبة) :69 د. ل / طماطم ميجور(24 علبة) :48 د. ل / طماطم الجيد(12 علبة) :24 د. ل ...'. Every item drops the word معجون and keeps only 'طماطم + brand'. A customer replies in the same bare form: 'طماطم الجيد خديناه امس ب 21 ونص علاش الفرق ف السعر'. CONCLUSION: Libyans do NOT reliably add a container word to the string itself — the header carries it once and the line items inherit it. So the string in isolation genuinely is undecidable, and the fix is not a container-word rule but a BRAND GAZETTEER plus two numeric tells: (1) a count-of-tins unit — (24 علبة), (12 علبة), ستيكة, قوطية, دسته, كارتون — is paste; (2) قابية, درجة أولى/ثانية, or a per-kilo price is fresh. Price magnitude also separates them in 2026: fresh runs 2–13 LYD per kg while a paste tin runs 1–3 LYD, so a 'طماطم X بـ2.5 دينار' with no unit is more likely a tin than a kilo, but this is probabilistic, not decisive.

Across five targeted searches (site:facebook.com Libya + هريسة + price/shop terms; Libyan online stores; Libyan food-trader groups; canned/factory harissa) the Libyan commercial web returns almost nothing: two of those searches returned ZERO organic results. What dominates instead is (a) home-cooking recipe content — 'الهريسة الليبية -بطريقة احترافية', 'هريسة من الصفر وبأبسط طريقة ... بتغنيكم عن الجاهز وما في داعي تشتروها بعد اليوم' ('this saves you from the ready-made kind, no need to ever buy it again'), 'الهريسه على الطريقه الليبيه المقادير ١ كيلو فلفل احمر حار'; and (b) EGYPTIAN e-commerce selling Libyan-style harissa to expatriates (karimolive.shop, bonomar.com, wa7et-siwa.com, amazon.eg) priced in EGP, which is not Libyan retail. notebook_question.finding: كراسة and دفتر are NOT synonyms in Libyan retail. Libyan stationery shops file them as two different product categories. مكتبة السفير (Tripoli, .ly storefront) has a category 'كراسات و مذكرات' with 243 products, and a separate category 'اوراق و دفاتر ملاحظات' with 45, plus 'السجلات والدفاتر' under office supplies. A shopper looking for a school exercise book goes to the كراسات shelf; دفتر sits with the loose-leaf pads and record books.

notebook_question.finding: THE CLINCHER — same shop, same page count, 4.4x the price. riad.ly (Libyan store, prices in د.ل) sells 'كراسة 100 ورقة مسطرة' at 2.50 د.ل and 'دفتر ملاحظات عربي 100 ورقة' at 11.00 د.ل. Both are 100 sheets. The price gap is not page count and not quality drift — it is two different products. Decisively, the دفتر listing uses الكراسة as its own size yardstick ('حجم ورقة الكراسة' = the size of a كراسة page), which only makes sense if the shop and its customers treat كراسة and دفتر as distinct, contrasting things.

Where a Libyan shop does sell a دفتر product, it is a refill pad: 'دفتر ورق مسطر مخرم 50 ورقة' at 6.00 د.ل for FEWER sheets than a 1.25 د.ل كراسة of 60 sheets. Fewer pages, 4.8x the price.

notebook_question.finding: The ~7x gap the catalogue observed is therefore real and structural, and it lines up almost exactly: كراسة spans roughly 0.50–4.0 LYD (0.50 قرش market offers up to a 100-page ruled book), دفتر spans roughly 3–11 LYD. Treating them as synonyms averages two different products and will mis-cost the school basket by 4–7x in either direction.
